issues.description: Twenty-one computable Section 05 rules encode only a sign or nakshatra while the exact source requires a planetary phase/event: मंगलोदय (R05-129, R05-130, R05-132, R05-133, R05-134, R05-136), मंगलास्त (R05-141, R05-143, R05-149), गुरु उदय/अस्त (R05-276, R05-277, R05-278, R05-280), or शुक्रोदय (R05-332, R05-333, R05-334, R05-341, R05-342, R05-343, R05-345, R05-346). conditionMatches has no phase/visibility predicate, so these rules match outside the source condition and can present an incomplete source claim as active.
issues.suggested_fix: Downgrade to reference until an exact source-faithful phase/visibility predicate is implemented. Do not add an inferred phase correction. If later supported, encode the phase and retain the stated sign/nakshatra as an AND condition.

issues.description: R05-343 and R05-345 also truncate explicit source nakshatra alternatives: R05-343 source says अनुराधा तथा ज्येष्ठा but metadata tests only ज्येष्ठा; R05-345 source says श्रवण, धनिष्ठा, शतभिषा, पूर्वा-भाद्रपद तथा उत्तरा-भाद्रपद but metadata tests only उत्तरा-भाद्रपद. Their phase condition is missing as well.
issues.suggested_fix: Downgrade to reference. Do not silently fill the missing values; only restore all source-stated alternatives after adding a faithful phase predicate and verifying the source block.

issues.description: R06-106 source requires मंगल in तुला राशि AND retrograde, but the condition contains only retrograde मंगल. R06-121 source requires गुरु in कर्क राशि AND retrograde, but the condition contains only retrograde गुरु. Both can therefore match in every sign.
issues.suggested_fix: Downgrade to reference unless the sign predicates are added exactly as stated: तुला for मंगल and कर्क for गुरु, joined with retrograde by AND.

issues.description: R05-167 summary preserves the source branch ‘यदि पाप-ग्रहों से युक्त’ (if joined/associated with malefics), but the computable condition is only बुध in वृषभ. The rule is shown as fully matched while that conditional branch is not evaluated.
issues.suggested_fix: Downgrade to reference unless the conditional branch is separately represented with a source-faithful conjunction predicate; do not fabricate a definition of ‘युक्त’.

issues.description: LocationFields mutates the live location state and the location pill changes immediately, but the existing snapshot and active-rule results remain from the old location until ‘स्थान लागू करें’ completes. During this interval the UI can label old astronomy as the newly selected location; Analysis also retains its initial from/to wall-clock state when the location timezone changes.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a draft location state and commit it together with a recalculation, or clear/mark the snapshot stale immediately on location edits. Reset or explicitly convert Analysis date fields when the timezone changes.

issues.description: Any calculation exception after partial progress sets runInfo.cancelled=true, so a failed partial run is labeled ‘अधूरा / रोका गया’ as if the user cancelled it. The error is shown, but the result status is semantically wrong.
issues.suggested_fix: Track completed, cancelled, and failed states separately; mark partial results as failed/partial when calculateAstro throws and reserve cancelled for cancel.current.

issues.description: The user-visible review overview says ‘कुल 1,778 नियम’, while the compiled dataset stats and the sum of its 14 section rule_count values are 1,822. Section-level counts otherwise reconcile. This creates a contradictory coverage claim in the Review page.
issues.suggested_fix: Regenerate or correct the overview text from the compiled dataset count; preserve the distinction between supplied-source coverage and executable coverage.

issues.description: The runtime canonical name is चंद्रमा, but the existing native astro test still searches for name === ‘चंद्र’ at line 51. If this script is run directly it fails the presence assertion despite the implementation using the corrected canonical name.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the test lookup to चंद्रमा (and keep all test fixtures aligned with the canonical planet-name map).
